name: Teeth
overview: Scripture uses teeth both literally and figuratively to convey spiritual realities, often associating them with the wicked and their opposition to the godly. The psalmist describes the breaking of the teeth of the ungodly as a sign of God's deliverance (Psalms 3:7), while the gnashing of teeth frequently symbolizes anger, hostility, or pain directed against the righteous (Job 16:9; Psalms 35:16; Psalms 37:12). Additionally, God's provision is pictured through the invitation to open the mouth wide to be filled, emphasizing His care and blessing (Psalms 81:10). Together, these verses reveal teeth as a biblical metaphor for both the aggression of the wicked and the sustaining grace of God toward His people.
